 Northern Virginia Man Charged in $200M International Student Loan Fraud Ring
 The man — a Kenyan national — allegedly used stolen identities to obtain $1.4 million in federal loans and grants. 
 By Debbie Williams • 
 Posted October 30, 2026 at 10:31 a.m. 
 Bill Doss/stock.adobe.com 
 A Northern Virginia man has been charged in the U.S. Justice Department’s “Operation Ghostbusters” investigation. 
 The DOJ says perpetrators created fraudulent Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) accounts using stolen U.S. citizen identities to enroll “ghost students” at colleges and universities. After the loan and grant money was disbursed, DOJ says it was “diverted to bank accounts controlled by foreign actors and facilitated by U.S.-based money mules, including Kenyan nationals.”
 Advertisement 
 The FBI’s Richmond field office launched the investigation. It’s been tracking an estimated $200 million in fraudulent claims. The NoVA man — a Kenyan national — was not named in the sealed indictment. He’s accused in stealing more than $1.4 million in federal student aid.
 Advertisement 
 The DOJ has charged him with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and student aid fraud. According to the indictment, he “conspired with fraudsters in Kenya to obtain and use the stolen identities” and “acted as a U.S. based money mule for the transnational fraud conspiracy.”
 “The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia is proud to be a leading part of law enforcement’s use of innovative techniques to fight fraud: using data to expose crime hiding in plain sight, starting with criminals who stole federal student aid using the stolen identities of ‘ghost students,’” First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos for the Eastern District of Virginia said in a news release . “Together with the Department of Education’s Office of Inspector General, the FBI Richmond cyber squad has already uncovered hundreds of participants and hundreds of millions of dollars in stolen funds, sending approximately 50 referrals to 26 FBI field offices across the country, and we are just getting started.”
